findings.passage: Firearm ownership is an American tradition and a God given right to self-defense in enshrined on our constitution by the Second Amendment
findings.note: Statement quoted by a TV news story (News4Jax) on gun ownership as a fundamental right; says government may restrict it only when a person poses a credible threat to others' physical safety.

findings.passage: For instance, a man who is convicted of carrying a firearm without a permission slip from the government in another state who poses no danger to the community should not be disarmed or dragged to prison as a felon for exerting his right to self-defense
findings.note: Quoted by News4Jax; argues a person convicted only of carrying without a licence elsewhere should not be barred from owning a gun.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.passage: While Florida law barring dangerous felons from possessing firearms is constitutional, it may only be required to those who are a danger to the public. Not someone who should have never been a felon in the first place
findings.note: Quoted by News4Jax; says the felon-possession ban is valid only for dangerous people.

findings.motion: Supplemental brief in State v. Morgan (First District Court of Appeal), asking to reverse a felon-in-possession conviction
findings.note: The attorney general's office reversed its earlier defence of a felon-possession conviction (Sept. 2025 brief) and filed a 37-page brief saying disarming a nondangerous felon, here one convicted only of carrying without a licence in another state, does not fit historical tradition.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.passage: The upshot of Florida's law is that a 20-year-old single mom is powerless to purchase a firearm to defend herself and her child against a menacing ex-boyfriend,
findings.note: From the attorney general's office brief to the U.S. Supreme Court, as quoted in a news story, urging review and reversal of Florida's under-21 ban on buying long guns.
subjects: minimum age to buy a gun

findings.motion: 17-page brief urging U.S. Supreme Court to take NRA's appeal and strike down Florida's under-21 rifle/long-gun purchase ban (2018 law)
findings.note: The attorney general declined to defend the 2018 law (said so in March 2025) and filed a brief asking the Supreme Court to hear the case and find the ban unconstitutional.
subjects: minimum age to buy a gun

findings.passage: Glad DOJ has followed suit in the fight for Second Amendment rights of Americans who are old enough to sign up to defend our nation!
findings.note: Post quoted by a public radio story, welcoming a federal Justice Department opinion that the federal ban on dealer handgun sales to 18-20-year-olds is unconstitutional.
subjects: minimum age to buy a gun

findings.motion: Guidance to prosecutors and police to stop enforcing Florida's open-carry ban after McDaniels v. State
findings.note: News story: the attorney general told prosecutors and law enforcement not to arrest or try law-abiding citizens carrying a firearm visibly, said the First District ruling binds all trial courts, and said bans on guns in places like courthouses, polling places and schools remain.
